Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is a disease caused by the fungus Venturia inaequalis, causing dark, scabby lesions.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Remove infected leaves and dropped fruit. Apply protective fungicides like captan or sulfur in early spring.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Black rot is caused by a fungus and appears as light brown spots on leaves or rotting fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune out dead or diseased wood. Implement a fungicide spray program containing myclobutanil or captan.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A fungal disease causing yellow-orange spots on leaves.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Remove nearby cedar hosts. Use preventative fungicides like myclobutanil before spores spread in spring.

Apple___healthy.treatment: Maintain regular watering and fertilization schedules.

Blueberry___healthy.treatment: Ensure soil acidity remains optimal and maintain watering routines.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease creating white, powdery fungal growth on leaves.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Ensure good air circulation. Spray with sulfur or neem oil early in the season.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.treatment: Maintain regular watering and fertilization schedules.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Fungal disease causing rectangular, gray-to-tan lesions on corn leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Use disease-resistant hybrids and practice crop rotation. Consider fungicide application if severe.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: A fungus resulting in small, rusty red-brown pustules on leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Plant rust-resistant corn varieties. Fungicides can help if applied at early signs.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Fungal disease causing cigar-shaped gray-green lesions.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Tillage to bury residue and crop rotation. Use resistant corn hybrids.

Grape___Black_rot.description: Shows as small, light brown circular spots on leaves or black rotting berries.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Prune off infected canes. Employ proper canopy management for airflow and apply preventative fungicides.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Also known as Black Measles, caused by a complex of fungi resulting in necrotic leaf striping.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: Remove and burn infected vines or cordons. Trunk renewal is often necessary.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Fungal disease causing browning and drying of leaves.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides or mancozeb. Improve vineyard air circulation.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: A devastating bacterial disease causing mottled leaves and misshapen, green fruit. Spread by the Asian citrus psyllid.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: No cure exists. Infected trees must be removed and destroyed to prevent spread. Control psyllid populations.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing angular, dark leaf spots which eventually fall out, creating a 'shot-hole' appearance.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Plant resistant varieties. Copper and oxytetracycline sprays can provide some control.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacteria causing dark, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Use disease-free seeds and transplants. Apply copper sprays. Avoid overhead watering.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: The bell pepper leaf is healthy.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.treatment: Maintain regular watering and fertilization schedules.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease causing 'bullseye' patterned lesions, usually on older leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply fungicides like chlorothalonil. Ensure proper crop rotation and avoid overhead watering.

Potato___Late_blight.description: The aggressive devastating fungus responsible for the Irish Potato Famine. Causes fast-spreading irregular brown lesions.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Requires immediate aggressive fungicide application (e.g., chlorothalonil, mancozeb). Destroy infected plants immediately.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Fungus producing a white powdery growth over the surfaces of leaves.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Improve air circulation. Apply sulfur-containing sprays or neem oil early.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Causes irregular dark purple spots on leaves that later cause them to brown and curl.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Remove affected leaves. Make sure to rotate beds and apply fungicides preventatively.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial disease causing small, water-soaked spots on leaves.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Use copper-based bactericides combined with mancozeb. Avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease causing dark concentric ring spots on older leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Mulch the soil, remove infected lower leaves, and use preventative fungicides like chlorothalonil.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Severely damaging pathogen causing large, irregular dark, water-soaked spots.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Immediately remove and destroy affected plants. Apply reliable fungicides preventatively before disease begins.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Fungal disease starting as pale green spots on upper leaf surfaces and mold underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Increase air circulation, space plants out, and reduce greenhouse humidity. Use appropriate fungicides.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Fungus causing numerous small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove affected leaves heavily, mulch to prevent soil splashing, and apply protectant fungicidal sprays.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Tiny pests causing stippling (tiny yellow dots) on leaves, often forming webbing.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Spray plants with a strong stream of water. Use horticultural oils, insecticidal soaps, or specific miticides.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Causes dark target-like, concentric ring lesions on leaves and deep fruit rot.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Improve air circulation and use fungicides like chlorothalonil or mancozeb.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Virus transmitted by whiteflies causing severe yellowing and upward curling of leaves.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: Control whitefly populations strongly. Plant resistant varieties. Remove infected plants entirely.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Virus causing mottling, yellowing, and fern-like appearance of leaves.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No cure. Remove infected plants. Disinfect hands and gardening tools thoroughly, as it is easily spread mechanically.

Tomato___healthy.treatment: Maintain regular watering to the roots (not leaves) and support vines to keep them off the soil.
